Marta — thanks for sending this over and for the clear list. Short answers up front, then detail below so you have a snippet suitable for your binder.

Short summary (copy-paste friendly):
- By default, Redwood stores incoming requests (prompts and request metadata) and model responses for hosted API customers to support quality monitoring, rate limiting, and debugging.
- Model outputs are treated as persisted artifacts by default (they are accessible to the customer in logs and subject to the same retention policy as requests) unless a customer opts into a configured ephemeral mode or a dedicated private deployment.
- Default residency follows the customer region configured at account creation (US by default for Acme). Retention default: 45 days for interactive requests and associated responses; 90 days for aggregated telemetry/metrics.
- Account-level purge requests trigger our controlled erase workflow; we provide time-stamped confirmation and an audit trace for SOC2 evidence.

Below is the fuller explanation for your security team and suggested wording for the binder.

Full details:
1) What we store by default
- Request content: user-provided prompts and request headers (IP, SDK client id, request_id) are stored by default to support debugging, billing, fraud detection, and model quality evaluations.
- Generated outputs: the raw model answer and any structured output fields (e.g., function-call payloads) are stored by default and indexed with the originating request record.
- Derived metadata: token counts, latency, model version, and anonymized usage metrics are stored longer-term for cost and performance analytics.

2) Residency and regionalization
- Records are stored in the region tied to the customer account. For Acme, the default is us-west-2 storage/compute. We can configure EU or APAC residency for enterprise contracts.

3) Default retention windows (hosted API)
- Interactive request/response logs: 45 days (default).
- Aggregated telemetry and performance metrics: 90 days.
- Attachments and customer-uploaded artifacts follow the same regional retention unless otherwise specified in contract.

4) Erasure workflow and evidence
- Initiation: customer opens a support request with account identifier and scope (e.g., "delete all logs for project: acme-retail-prod").
- Validation: we authenticate requestor and catalogue affected keys/objects.
- Execution: background purge jobs remove records from primary stores and mark tombstones in archival indexes.
- Evidence: we provide a signed PDF audit record listing affected object ids, timestamps, and a job id. For legal/forensics we also provide S3 delete manifests where applicable.
- Timing: most purge jobs complete within 72 hours; depending on backups/replication there may be additional propagation of deletion (we include estimates in the job evidence).

5) Options to reduce persistence
- Ephemeral mode: an opt-in configuration for hosted customers that avoids persisting user prompts/outputs beyond the immediate request lifecycle (best-effort, subject to operational logs).
- Redwood Private / Dedicated: customers can run with a private control plane and storage under their account with bespoke retention and erase SLAs.

Marta — quick answers inline, and below is a sanitized PDF example you can drop into your binder.

1) Audit PDF fields: we include request_id(s), S3 object ids (where applicable), UTC deletion timestamp, purge job id, and operator/service account identity. We also include a short statement of scope (e.g., "Account-level purge for acme-retail-prod, objects created before 2026-04-27T00:00:00Z").

2) Backups: daily backups are retained for an additional 30 days by default. Our purge workflow schedules backup invalidation and overwrite; full propagation to all cold backups can take up to 35 days. We include this window in the audit evidence PDF. For enterprise contracts we can shorten this window or provide dedicated backup deletion SLAs.
